gold_answers.rubric_note: Creates one student object correctly but no array.

gold_answers.rubric_note: Creates full array of 4 students but no function.

gold_answers.rubric_note: Perfect. Fully commented, descriptive names, formatted output, function is clean and reusable.
gold_answers.code_answer: // Array of student objects with name and score const students = [   { name: "Nick", score: 85 },   { name: "Amy", score: 45 },   { name: "Tom", score: 72 },   { name: "Sara", score: 38 } ]; // Function returns only students scoring 70 or above function getTopStudents(studentArray) {   return studentArray.filter(student => student.score >= 70); } const topStudents = getTopStudents(students); console.log("Top Students (Distinction Level):"); topStudents.forEach(student => {   console.log(`${student.name}: ${student.score}/100`); });

learning_outcome: Students shall be able to implement error handling using try/catch blocks to manage exceptions in JavaScript programs.
question_text: Write a JavaScript function called divideNumbers(a, b) that divides a by b. If b is zero, it should throw an error with the message "Cannot divide by zero". Use a try/catch block when calling the function to handle the error and print an appropriate message to the console.

gold_answers.rubric_note: Attempts task but syntax completely wrong.
gold_answers.code_answer: function divide(a,b) { return a/b }

gold_answers.rubric_note: Function divides correctly but no error handling at all.
gold_answers.code_answer: function divideNumbers(a, b) {   return a / b; } console.log(divideNumbers(10, 2));

gold_answers.rubric_note: Has if check for zero but no throw, just returns or logs.
gold_answers.code_answer: function divideNumbers(a, b) {   if (b === 0) {     console.log("Cannot divide by zero");   }   return a / b; }

gold_answers.rubric_note: Throws error correctly but no try/catch when calling.
gold_answers.code_answer: function divideNumbers(a, b) {   if (b === 0) {     throw new Error("Cannot divide by zero");   }   return a / b; } divideNumbers(10, 0);

gold_answers.rubric_note: Has try/catch but error message in throw is wrong.
gold_answers.code_answer: function divideNumbers(a, b) {   if (b === 0) {     throw new Error("Error!");   }   return a / b; } try {   divideNumbers(10, 0); } catch (e) {   console.log(e.message); }

gold_answers.rubric_note: Correct throw message, try/catch works but catch just logs e not e.message.
gold_answers.code_answer: function divideNumbers(a, b) {   if (b === 0) {     throw new Error("Cannot divide by zero");   }   return a / b; } try {   divideNumbers(10, 0); } catch (e) {   console.log(e); }

gold_answers.rubric_note: Fully correct — throws right message, try/catch catches and prints e.message.
gold_answers.code_answer: function divideNumbers(a, b) {   if (b === 0) {     throw new Error("Cannot divide by zero");   }   return a / b; } try {   const result = divideNumbers(10, 0);   console.log("Result:", result); } catch (e) {   console.log("Error:", e.message); }

gold_answers.rubric_note: Correct, tests both a valid call and an invalid call.
gold_answers.code_answer: function divideNumbers(a, b) {   if (b === 0) {     throw new Error("Cannot divide by zero");   }   return a / b; } try {   console.log(divideNumbers(10, 2));   console.log(divideNumbers(10, 0)); } catch (e) {   console.log("Error caught:", e.message); }

gold_answers.rubric_note: Correct, clean, uses finally block as well.
gold_answers.code_answer: function divideNumbers(a, b) {   if (b === 0) {     throw new Error("Cannot divide by zero");   }   return a / b; } try {   const result = divideNumbers(10, 0);   console.log("Result:", result); } catch (e) {   console.log("Error caught:", e.message); } finally {   console.log("Division attempted."); }

gold_answers.rubric_note: Perfect. Comments, correct throw, try/catch/finally, tests valid and invalid cases, clean readable code.
gold_answers.code_answer: // Function to safely divide two numbers function divideNumbers(a, b) {   // Check for division by zero   if (b === 0) {     throw new Error("Cannot divide by zero");   }   return a / b; } // Test with valid input try {   const result = divideNumbers(10, 2);   console.log("10 / 2 =", result); } catch (e) {   console.log("Error:", e.message); } // Test with invalid input (division by zero) try {   const result = divideNumbers(10, 0);   console.log("Result:", result); } catch (e) {   console.log("Error caught:", e.message); } finally {   console.log("Operation complete."); }

gold_answers.rubric_note: Perfect. Fully commented, uses arrow functions, tests multiple operations, shows reusability of higher-order function clearly.
gold_answers.code_answer: // Higher-order function that applies any operation to each element function applyOperation(numbers, operation) {   // Map applies the operation function to every number   return numbers.map(operation); } // Operation functions const double = n => n * 2;   // Doubles the number const square = n => n * n;   // Squares the number const triple = n => n * 3;   // Triples the number const numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]; // Test with different operations console.log("Original:", numbers); console.log("Doubled:", applyOperation(numbers, double)); console.log("Squared:", applyOperation(numbers, square)); console.log("Tripled:", applyOperation(numbers, triple));
